title: Hightower Insurance - renewal & scaling roadmap sync
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in to align on capacity uplift, EU+APAC onboarding timeline, and contract extension terms. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency on claims-processing models but wants Private/VPC option for a subset of PII workloads. Action items: pricing spreadsheet, security SOC2 artifacts, pilot plan for EU region.
topics: Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst behavior
EU and APAC region onboarding timeline
SLA and latency SLOs for claims models
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~44m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sofia (Hightower), Daniel (Platform Eng), Liam (Procurement)

[00:00:05] Alex (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Uh, quick agenda — run through where usage is, talk about the renewal numbers, and the region onboarding timeline, and then open Q&A. Sofia, is this still a good set?

[00:00:22] Sofia (Hightower): Yeah, sounds good. Um, and thanks — we've got the team ready. Daniel and I will jump in on the infra bits, Liam is here for procurement timeline and terms.

[00:00:37] Alex: Great. Quick check — last quarter you were averaging about 2.1B tokens/month with spikes to 3.4B during claims runs, right? I pulled the dashboard.

[00:00:48] Priya (Redwood SE): yep that's what our telemetry shows; and latency percentiles were around 180ms p95 on hosted, but for the claims model specifically the p95 drifted to 280ms during peak with batching on.

[00:01:02] Daniel: Yeah, that's the problem — for latency-sensitive workflows we need something more predictable. We tried more aggressive batching but it hurts SLA.

[00:01:12] Sofia: So our question 1 is capacity: do we move to Dedicated reserved GPU pools for the claims model, and how fast can you provision EU region nodes?

[00:01:25] Alex: Ok, two parts. Dedicated gives you the predictable throughput and isolation; our Dedicated customers usually see p95 down to 80-120ms depending on model and sequence length. EU provisioning: we can start a pilot in 2–3 weeks if you sign the SOW, full ramp ~6–8 weeks depending on capacity commit.

[00:01:46] Liam: For procurement, what's the minimum term for Dedicated? We were thinking 12 months, but do you do quarterly ramp options?

[00:01:58] Alex: Standard is 12 months for reserved capacity, but we can do a 6-month pilot with a conversion credit toward the annual commit. We'll follow up in the pricing spreadsheet.

[00:02:12] Priya: From the technical side, if you want to keep PII workloads on-prem or in a VPC, Redwood Private supports a hybrid model — control plane managed, runtime in your VPC, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key isolation.

[00:02:26] Daniel: Important — the regulatory folks insist on keys never leaving our HSM, and audit logs for inference calls. Is that supported?

[00:02:35] Priya: Yes, HSM integrations are standard in Private deployments; audit logs with request-level tracing are available and we can increase retention. Note: for Private we do a separate licensing fee + support tier.

[00:02:50] Sofia: Can you clarify data at rest encryption vs in transit? Our security team asks for specifics.

[00:02:56] Alex: TLS in transit, and AES-256 for data at rest; for Private you can bring your own KMS and HSM for key wraps. We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs.

[00:03:08] Liam: Please send the SOC 2 report and the penetration test summary to procurement, that will unblock our legal review.

[00:03:15] Alex: Absolutely, we'll share that after the call.

[00:03:22] Daniel: Back to latency vs cost tradeoff — you mentioned quantization options? Will that affect model quality for claim classification?

[00:03:30] Priya: Good question. We recommend per-workload quant profiles: for classification models you can often go to int8 or q4 depending on model family; Redwood Optimize suggests profiles based on your evals. There's a small quality delta, we can run an eval set to quantify.

[00:03:47] Sofia: We need a formal eval — can Redwood run the benchmark on our test set in EU?

[00:03:52] Priya: Yes — we can run a short benchmark as part of the pilot, using either Hosted EU test instances or Dedicated pilot nodes. We'll capture latency/cost/accuracy.

[00:04:05] Alex: Let's talk numbers — currently your baseline commit suggestion on the sheet is 10 reserved GPUs equivalent with burst. Does that still fit your forecast?

[00:04:15] Daniel: We forecast growth to 15 GPUs by Q4 with more daytime spikes. We want autoscaling but predictable baseline.

[00:04:24] Priya: The autoscaling policy can be configured: baseline reserved capacity with a burst pool for sudden spikes. There's also smart routing to route less-sensitive requests to cheaper model variants or lower-cost regions.

[00:04:38] Sofia: We like that. Is smart routing something we could use to route anonymized/low-sensitivity traffic to hosted cheaper region?

[00:04:45] Alex: Yep, policy-based routing supports that — tag requests and route by sensitivity. Good for cost saving.

[00:04:53] Daniel: Timeline again for EU pilot?

[00:04:55] Alex: 2–3 weeks to stand up pilot nodes once SOW is signed; we can do a two-week benchmark window. Full multi-AZ production ~6–8 weeks. APAC provisioning typically adds another 3–4 weeks depending on capacity.

[00:05:12] Sofia: For APAC we need data residency in Singapore for certain regulatory customers; can you host there?

[00:05:18] Priya: Yes, we have APAC capacity plans and partner regions; we need an explicit commit for APAC to prioritize capacity.

[00:05:25] Liam: On pricing — what's the uplift for Private vs Dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine for now.

[00:05:32] Alex: Ballpark: Dedicated reserved pricing per GPU hour, Private adds platform license and higher support — like a percent uplift (we'll put exact tiers in the spreadsheet). Also, longer term commitments reduce unit price.

[00:05:44] Daniel: Any competitors mentioned here — we've seen BigCloudAI and ModelServePro in procurement RFPs; their managed offerings claim lower cost but not the same observability.

[00:05:56] Priya: Yeah, BigCloudAI tends to be cheaper for bulk tokens but less optimized for on-prem/private workflows; ModelServePro has a self-hosted story but requires more ops from your side.

[00:06:10] Sofia: Another question: rollouts. We need canary and automatic fallback if a new model regresses. How does Redwood handle that?

[00:06:17] Priya: Rollouts are first-class: you can do canary, A/B, and automatic fallback based on quality monitors tied to your evals and synthetic traffic. If quality drops, routing falls back to previous model.

[00:06:30] Daniel: Great. For the pilot we'll need instrumentation hooks to send logs to our Splunk — is that supported?

[00:06:36] Priya: Yes, we have log forwarding and tracing hooks, and token-level cost breakdowns so you can send them to Splunk or DataDog.

[00:06:44] Sofia: Ok, procurement question — if we sign the SOW this month, when do you need PO and billing start?

[00:06:50] Alex: Typical: PO within 14 days of SOW, billing starts on provisioning date. For a pilot you can do an initial invoice for the pilot period, then convert.

[00:06:59] Liam: Our legal will want indemnity language and a subprocessor list. Also, an explicit SLA for p95 latency for claims-critical endpoints.

[00:07:08] Alex: We'll include subprocessor list and SLA language in the contract draft. SLA targets for Dedicated we can set in the SOW — e.g., 100ms p95 for certain model configs; exact SLO depends on model and sequence length.

[00:07:21] Daniel: On the SLO measurement: do you provide synthetic canary checks or should we run our own?

[00:07:26] Priya: Both — we provide synthetic healthchecks and you can push synthetic traffic. We'll correlate our telemetry with your traces.

[00:07:34] Sofia: Let's talk pilot scope: 2 GPUs in EU for two weeks, run benchmark, then scale to 6 GPUs for canary. Does that sound realistic?

[00:07:43] Priya: Yes that works. We'll define the exact instance types in the SOW. We'll also run quantization tests and a latency-quality matrix.

[00:07:53] Alex: Next steps — we'll send pricing + SOW template, SOC2 and penetration test summary, and a pilot schedule. Also, we'll schedule a technical deep dive with engs next week.

[00:08:05] Liam: Sounds good. Procurement will review the documents; expect back in 10 business days.

[00:08:12] Sofia: One last item — can you confirm support hours for APAC?

[00:08:16] Alex: Support for APAC can be included in higher support tiers; but we can guarantee 24x7 coverage for P1 with enterprise support. We'll put the explicit SLAs in the contract appendix.

[00:08:27] Daniel: Ok thanks.

[00:08:30] Alex: Great, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with materials.

[00:08:33] Sofia: Thanks all.
